title: Signed GPU Runtime Bundle and Verifier Guidelines
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines the standard for producing cryptographically signed GPU runtime bundles (images + runtime patches + kernel module blobs) and the runtime verifier that guarantees only authorized, reproducible bundles run on Redwood GPU nodes. The goals are: enforce supply-chain integrity, enable fast incident rollbacks, and provide automated verification during node bootstrap and runtime updates.

Scope

- Applies to all production GPU node images and GPU-specific runtime bundles ("gpu-runtime-bundle") used by: Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Includes build signing in CI, artifact storage, KMS-managed signing keys, verifier integration in node bootstrap, and monitoring/alerts.
- Excludes ephemeral developer test images unless explicitly gate-kept by release process.

Ownership and Stakeholders

- Primary owner: eng-infra (CI/CD & Build team)
- Security owner: security-and-compliance (for key rotation policy and audit)
- Runtime owner: eng-serving-runtime (integration for verifier hooks)
- Oncall escalation: eng-sre (pager rota for verification alerts)

Definitions

- gpu-runtime-bundle: tar.gz containing OS rootfs layer, GPU driver/kernel-module artifacts, curated runtime binaries (redwood-gpu-runtime), and a manifest.json describing checksums and provenance.
- Signed manifest: manifest.json + signature (cosign format) stored alongside bundle in Artifact Registry.

High-level Requirements

1) All production-ready gpu-runtime-bundles must be signed with a KMS-backed key before being published to artifact-registry.redwood.internal.
2) Node bootstrap must verify signature prior to mounting rootfs and before starting redwood-gpu-runtime. Failure to verify must halt GPU enabling and mark node as degraded.
3) Signing process must embed build provenance: CI job id, git commit, builder image digest, and SBOM link.
4) Verification latency target: cold verify at bootstrap <= 500ms (p95), warm verify (cached keys) <= 50ms (p95).
5) Signing and verification audit logs must be retained for 1 year and forwarded to security SIEM.

CI/CD Signing Pipeline (recommended implementation)

- Build job name: ci/gpu-image-builder/release
- Steps:
  1. Build rootfs and runtime artifacts.
  2. Produce manifest.json with SHA256 digests for every file. Example manifest snippet:

    {
      "bundle_version": "2026-02-20-rc1",
      "components": [
        {
          "path": "/opt/redwood/bin/redwood-gpu-runtime",
          "sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924..."
        }
      ],
      "build_provenance": {
        "ci_job": "ci/gpu-image-builder/release/853",
        "git_commit": "a1b2c3d4",
        "builder_image": "gcr.io/redwood/builders/gpu-builder@sha256:..."
      }
    }

  3. Use cosign (sigstore) to sign manifest: cosign sign --key ksvc://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/signing/cryptoKeys/gpu-bundles manifest.json
  4. Push bundle.tar.gz, manifest.json, and manifest.json.sig to artifact-registry.redwood.internal/gpu-bundles/<version>/
  5. Emit provenance metadata to build index service (POST /internal/build-index).

Example CI YAML snippet (GitLab-style):

  stages:
    - build
    - sign
    - publish

  build_bundle:
    stage: build
    script:
      - ./tools/build-gpu-bundle.sh --out ./dist/bundle.tar.gz
      - ./tools/generate-manifest.py --out ./dist/manifest.json ./dist/bundle.tar.gz

  sign_manifest:
    stage: sign
    script:
      - cosign sign --key ksvc://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/signing/cryptoKeys/gpu-bundles ./dist/manifest.json
    needs: [build_bundle]

  publish_artifact:
    stage: publish
    script:
      - gsutil cp ./dist/* gs://artifact-registry.redwood.internal/gpu-bundles/${CI_COMMIT_TAG:-${CI_COMMIT_SHA}}/
    needs: [sign_manifest]

KMS and Key Management

- Primary signing key lives in KMS (AWS KMS CMK or GCP KMS based on region). Use an HSM-backed asymmetric key for signing.
- Key identifiers must be recorded in the manifest (kms_key: projects/.../cryptoKeys/...).
- Key rotation: quarterly scheduled rotation with overlap window of 72 hours. Old keys remain usable for verification for a 30-day grace period. Security must approve rotation and publish rotation events to audit-log.

Runtime Verifier Integration

- Component name: runtime-bundle-verifier (binary shipped in node-bootstrap image)
- Startup path: systemd unit runs /usr/local/bin/runtime-bundle-verifier verify --bundle /var/lib/gpu/bundle.tar.gz --manifest /var/lib/gpu/manifest.json
- Verification steps:
  1. Fetch signature and manifest from local artifact path or /etc/verified-bundles cache.
  2. Verify signature against KMS key via sigstore/cosign verifying library with KMS connector.
  3. Recompute SHA256s against unpacked files and compare to manifest.
  4. If verification fails, call /internal/node-health/set-degraded --reason="bundle-verification-failed" and stop GPU service.

Example runtime verification CLI (pseudo):

  /usr/local/bin/runtime-bundle-verifier verify --manifest /var/lib/gpu/manifest.json --sig /var/lib/gpu/manifest.json.sig --key-id projects/redwood/.../gpu-bundles

Performance and caching

- Keep a local KMS public-key cache and manifest cache to avoid remote KMS/API calls on every verify.
- Metrics to emit:
  - infra.signedbundle.verify.latency_ms (histogram)
  - infra.signedbundle.verify.failure_count (counter)
  - infra.signedbundle.verify.cache_hit (counter)
- Alert conditions:
  - infra.signedbundle.verify.failure_count > 5 within 5m in a single region -> P1 to eng-sre
  - p95(infra.signedbundle.verify.latency_ms) > 500ms for > 10 minutes -> P2

Rollout and Canary Strategy

1. Start with a canary fleet of 5–10 nodes in us-west1. Configure nodes with extra logging and a temporary bypass flag that only security staff can toggle.
2. Monitor verify.failure_count and node_degraded_count for 24h.
3. Expand to 20% of cluster capacity on green signals.
4. Full rollout after 72h of stable metrics.
5. Rollback: revert node bootstrap service configuration to previous bundle source and mark affected nodes for reimage; ensure CI retains the last-known-good signed bundle tag.

Developer and QA Test Matrix

- Unit tests: manifest generation, signature validator, key rotation handling.
- Integration tests: sign+publish+verify round-trip in ephemeral GKE cluster with simulated KMS.
- Chaos tests: simulate KMS throttling, broken manifests, partial bundles, and ensure node-degraded flows trigger correct alerts and do not fallback to unsigned bundles.

Terraform / IaC Modules and Example Resources

- Module: terraform-modules/gpu_artifact_bucket (creates artifact storage with uniform access policy, lifecycle rule, and object versioning)
- Module: terraform-modules/kms_signing_key (provisions KMS asymmetric key, IAM bindings for CI principal, and rotation schedule)
- Module variables to enforce:
  - enforce_signed_bundles=true
  - artifact_bucket_retention_days=400

Example TF snippet to use signing key in CI role binding:

  resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "ci_signer" {
    crypto_key_id = module.kms_signing_key.crypto_key_id
    role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
    member        = "serviceAccount:ci-pipelines@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  }

Operational Playbook (runbook)

- Symptom: new nodes come up degraded with reason "bundle-verification-failed"
- Immediate steps:
  1. Check infra.signedbundle.verify.failure_count for region and time window.
  2. Verify the manifest.json and manifest.json.sig exist in artifact registry for the bundle tag.
  3. Confirm KMS key status (not disabled/rotated) and examine key-rotation events in audit-log.
  4. If CI recently rotated key: trigger emergency verifier update to accept previous key while rotating caches.
  5. If bundle is corrupt: mark bundle as revoked in artifact registry and trigger reimage of affected nodes with last-known-good bundle.
  6. Pager to eng-sre and security on any unsigned-production-bundle or key compromise suspicion.

Post-incident analysis checklist:

- Collect: verifier logs, vault/KMS audit events, CI job logs, artifact bucket object metadata, and node bootstrap logs.
- Determine root cause: signing bug, artifact corruption, KMS outage, or verifier regression.
- Action items: patch CI, rotate keys if compromised, publish a remediation timeline, and update runbook with the new troubleshooting step.

Audit and Compliance

- Ensure signed-manifest audit entries are forwarded to SIEM with fields: bundle_version, git_commit, signer_key_id, timestamp, CI_job_id.
- Retention: 1 year for audit entries, 400 days for artifacts by default.
- Generate monthly report for security-and-compliance showing counts of signed bundles and verification failures.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Links

- Verify locally using cosign with KMS connector:
  cosign verify --key ksvc://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/signing/cryptoKeys/gpu-bundles gs://artifact-registry.redwood.internal/gpu-bundles/2026-02-20-rc1/manifest.json

- Runtime verifier (debug):
  /usr/local/bin/runtime-bundle-verifier verify --manifest /var/lib/gpu/manifest.json --debug --output /tmp/verify.log

- Observability dashboards:
  - infra -> Signed Bundles (p95 latency, failures by region, cache-hit rate)

- Related policies:
  - Key rotation policy: security-and-compliance/key-rotation-policy-2025
  - Artifact retention policy: finance-and-legal/artifact-retention-2024
